title: Kipple is out on Steam: a free desktop pet dreamed by local AI, with checks that reject bad dreams
author: Impossible_Heat5748
selftext:
I'm the developer of Kipple, a free desktop companion and creature collector for Windows, now released on Steam. The creature artwork and dialogue are generated by AI models bundled with the game and running on the player's PC. Your Kipple lives over the desktop, reacts to petting, naps, chats and remembers notes from your conversations.



The part that may interest this community is turning a generated image into something the game can actually use. A local LLM writes the creature's description and personality from game-authored species, palette and trait recipes. SDXL through stable-diffusion.cpp paints it on a white canvas, then the pipeline removes the background and checks the result before it reaches the desktop. Checks can reject clipped limbs, leftover background or unusable eyes; vision checks also look at the species. The finished artwork gets a blink rig and runtime expressions.



Generating a nice picture is only one step: it also needs to cut out cleanly and work with the animation. Rejected attempts mean a dream can take several minutes, depending on hardware. The game ships its AI runtime, so players don't need an API key or AI subscription. Chat and memory files stay local; creature artwork and item metadata go online for moderation and Steam inventory delivery.



Hardware: Windows 10/11, 16 GB RAM and 20 GB storage; a Vulkan-capable GPU with 6 GB or more VRAM is recommended.



Kipple is free to play here: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/3120010/Kipple/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=oct26&utm\_content=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3120010/Kipple/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=oct26&utm_content=aigamedev)



For other developers shipping local generation: how are you handling retries without making the wait frustrating? Happy to discuss the pipeline.
